highlights: Your Claude subscription now runs Claude Code 2.1.322, where the fable alias picks Claude Fable 5.2.
Your Assistant can search the web and read pages, once you switch on its web tools.
AI Review reads each search result and page with your TypeSafe key before the Assistant sees it.
A model that keeps repeating the same call is told to reach its goal another way, and the run goes on.
The receipt counts how many times that happened (usage.loopNudges).
Your organization can set your Assistant's name and personality.
It can also add MCP servers and knowledge packs to your persistent agents.
A QuickAgent your organization assigns with a model runs on your saved model of it, unless you pick another.
Persistent agents' web tools and AI Review work when your organization pays for them with its credits.
QuickAgents your organization requires are installed for you, and their first run still asks you.
agentry search --org lists the QuickAgents your organization offers.
A QuickAgent your organization requires can't be uninstalled while it is required.
QuickAgents that ship skills run as in 0.7.47, now on Agentry's v0.7.12 core release.
A QuickAgent can ship skills: folders of instructions it reads when a step of its task matches one.
Installing a QuickAgent that ships skills says so before you agree.
Your organization's managed settings can now choose or limit the model provider, the model and the coding tools.
agentry setup fills in the model your organization sets, and skips that step when the organization locks it.
An AI Review or web search key your organization provides is kept in your keychain and never shown.
If your organization pays for AI Review or web search with its credits, you need no key of your own for them.
When a run answers with steps of its checklist still open, Agentry asks it to finish them or say why not.
Agentry asks at most twice, and the run's result records how its checklist ended.
When a long run summarizes earlier work, the summary keeps the task, the checklist and the next step.
A run now keeps the steps of its task in a checklist, which it reads again after a summary and before it answers.
The checklist is a working note in the run's scratch folder and never reaches your reports.
You can move a schedule on a runhost to another saved model it holds, without making the schedule again.
Nothing of this computer's goes with the move: the runhost reads the model and its key from its own store.
The Assistant reads the files of a QuickAgent it fetches in the same reply, without waiting for your next message.
Those files are still checked first, for malware too when the malware check is on.
Every security setting your organization manages now applies to your runs, not only Unsafe Mode.
A lock holds even if you edit your policy file, and a refused run names your organization and the setting.
Caps on a run's time, turns and cost lower your budgets; your own lower limits stay.
Your organization can set where runs go, which QuickAgents install, schedules and the oldest Agentry that runs.
The Assistant has new tools to list, fetch, revise, fork and submit the QuickAgents you publish.
Agentry Desktop answers those tools in a coming update, asking you before each change; until then they say so.
A new QuickAgent the Assistant submits is private, and it cannot delete a QuickAgent or make one public.
agentry providers now lists, signs in again and removes your model sign-ins; agentry model-signins is deprecated.
When the registry rotates its signing key and the old key hands over to the new one, Agentry trusts the new key itself.
A new key with no handover from a key you pinned is still only reported, never trusted on the registry's word.
Your organization's managed settings keep reaching you after a key rotation, signed by the new key.
A lock on a managed setting this version does not apply yet stops runs and names the update, never silently ignored.
agentry run --model runs a QuickAgent on any saved model, and a schedule keeps the model you give it with --model.
agentry agent configure --model puts a persistent agent on a saved model, and a running agent takes it at its next turn.
agentry runhost model --add makes a saved model available on a runhost, checked there, for its agents and schedules.
Receipts name the saved model, and one that is gone or lacks its key or sign-in is refused, never run on the default.
A schedule made in Agentry Desktop's Unsafe Mode waits while your organization forbids Unsafe Mode, then runs again.
schedule list and schedule show say when your organization's managed settings hold a schedule.
agentry providers and agentry models keep up to 10 saved models, each a provider and a model id; one is the default.
A saved model is checked when you save it, and an endpoint of your own fills in its context window.
Switching computer use or an application on or off for a persistent agent takes effect at its next turn.
An agent no longer fails every start with computer use after you switch computer use off for it.
A QuickAgent can name any application on your computer; Agentry Desktop resolves it to one you approved there.
An application's tools come from Agentry Desktop when the run starts, with the class it gives each tool.
desktop.allowCustomServers in the policy now defaults to on; Unsafe Mode allows your own applications under false.
agentry doctor lists the applications you set up in Agentry Desktop, once Agentry Desktop lists them.
If your organization manages your settings, the CLI fetches them at sign-in, checks their signature and follows them.
agentry managed show lists the settings your organization holds you to; agentry managed refresh fetches them again.
agentry publish says what happened and where to look, with distinct exit codes and a --json answer.
agentry validate names the stages it did not run, and refuses lines left over from the scaffold.
The Assistant can use applications on your computer, such as Blender, once you switch each one on.
A switch takes effect at the agent's next turn; opening or closing the application restarts nothing.
Code the agent runs inside an application asks you first, unless you switch on its own agreement.
An agent on your runhost reaches your computer through Agentry Desktop while it runs.
A QuickAgent that uses an application on your computer can run on your own runhost with --on.
Agentry Desktop on this computer answers the run's calls while you follow it; if this computer leaves, they are refused.
agentry runhost attach links the run to this computer again.
A run that used an application on your computer and then failed still counts, in its receipt, the calls that crossed.
A QuickAgent can use Unreal Engine on your computer through Epic's own Unreal MCP plugin, with Agentry Desktop.
When something in front of the registry refuses a request with a web page, the error names the page and its ray id.
A run that does computer use keeps no screenshot in its receipts, its event log included.
A QuickAgent can now see and use the windows of an application on your computer, through Agentry Desktop.
It works in the windows you allow and nowhere else; a QuickAgent that asks for your whole screen needs --allow-screen.
The receipt names the scope and what Agentry Desktop says your computer held; the run keeps no screenshot.
A long autonomous run keeps its place and its findings in notes.md in its scratch folder.
After the harness summarises earlier work, the agent reads its notes first and carries on from where they say.
A report design built from your document takes its logo, its cover photograph or artwork, and a cover modelled on yours.
No whole page of your document and none of its text is kept in the design.
A QuickAgent can use Blender on your own computer through its installed MCP server, from inside its sandbox.
Each call reaches Agentry Desktop, which must be running, and a hosted run never has it.
A run on a model server of your own asks the server for the model's context window when the policy records none.
The run uses the window it finds for that run only, says where it came from, and leaves the policy as it is.
An autonomous run resumes its conversation when the model server fails after its first tool call.
It waits 30 seconds to 2 minutes, at most five times, and never past the run's timeout; no tool runs twice.
agentry report-design design --document builds a design around a PDF or Word document of yours.
The Report Designer looks at a PDF's first twelve pages and reads a Word document's theme, header, footer and pictures.
It takes your logo from the document when you give none, and the document is kept only for the run.
A run on your own model server summarizes and goes on when the server says it is too long, window known or not.
Your own model server has 30 minutes to start answering a long prompt before a run gives up; hosted models keep 5.
A reminder the Assistant's task sends reaches you as a message from it, apart from the task's own work.
agentry agent chat shows that message in full, while the task's own work stays faint.
agentry report-design design writes a whole report design from your brief, logo, reference images and web pages.
agentry report-design cover writes a custom cover page for one of your designs, looking at each render it makes.
With --save, what the Report Designer makes joins your account's designs under a new name, never as your default.
A PDF draws a design's custom cover as its first page, and falls back to the band cover if the cover fails.
PDF reports take a whole brand: a running header, a three-slot footer, your contact lines and a cover in six styles.
Ten built-in report designs, five of them new: Boardroom, Studio, Field, Civic and Lumen.
agentry run --report-design picks a library design by name; report-design list, use and delete manage the library.
An earlier report design file is refused by its version; export it again from your account, which holds them all anew.
The Assistant's set-up steps for Google, Microsoft 365, Fastmail and calendar feeds no longer ask you to stop it.
A run on a model of your own reads files in pages sized to the model's context window, 16 KiB to 48 KiB.
On a model of your own, older tool results give way once they pass half the window, or 64k tokens if it is unknown.
A model of your own compacts its conversation at 70% of its window, not 90%.
A running persistent agent takes a change to the runner's policy, its model and harness included, at its next turn.
agentry agent install updates a running persistent agent: it takes the new release at its next turn.
agentry agent uninstall and reset stop a running agent first, rather than refusing.
A running agent on an older Agentry is handed over to the new one between turns, its conversation kept.
Google Workspace's and Microsoft 365's set-ups and sign-ins work while the Assistant runs.
The agent pauses between turns while one is set up, then goes on with it, its conversation kept.
agentry agent show says what a paused agent is being set up with.
Mail providers, Microsoft 365's app and signoff, a Fastmail token and calendar feeds change while an agent runs.
A running persistent agent takes each of them at its next turn, without a stop and a start.
agentry agent disable stops a running agent first, rather than refusing.
A server, pack or secret added to a running persistent agent that keeps it from starting is switched off, not fatal.
agentry agent show names what a running agent switched off that way, and why.
A knowledge pack built again reaches a running persistent agent at its next turn, with no stop and start.
Saving the Coding agent's dev server again, with a new sign-in, applies at its next turn.
agentry agent show marks a server, pack or dev server pending while a running agent waits to take its change.
agentry agent messenger takes --on: an agent on your remote runhost answers its messengers while your computer is off.
Talk to a running persistent agent from Discord, Slack or Matrix as well as Telegram: agentry agent messenger add.
agentry agent start, chat and stop take --on to run the Assistant on your remote runhost.
The Assistant summarises a call whose other voices Agentry Desktop told apart, keeping each as Speaker 1, 2 and so on.
agentry agent secret set and configure --account take --on, keeping the value in the runhost's store.
A persistent agent on Claude Code whose stored conversation is gone starts on a new one instead of failing.
agentry install --local over an unreadable installed.yaml installs and rewrites the record.
agentry --json run prints the failure envelope when a run fails before it has a result.
agentry schedule add --check with --on says what a runhost's schedule would keep there, keeping nothing.
agentry agent messenger add and pair let you talk to a running persistent agent from your own Telegram bot.
agentry schedule add --on lab runs a QuickAgent on the runhost named lab on repeat, with nobody present.
A runhost keeps a schedule's secrets in its store, under a key systemd seals to the server.
agentry runhost schedules lists a runhost's schedules and their runs, which runhost collect opens.
agentry runhost update brings runhosts to this CLI's version over their run keys; so does each CLI update.
agentry runhost pair adds another computer of yours to a runhost; unpair takes it off and revokes its credits token.
A runhost can be Fedora 43 or 44, or RHEL, AlmaLinux or Rocky Linux 9 or 10, as well as Debian or Ubuntu.
agentry setup asks a model server of your own for its context window, so long runs on it compact instead of failing.
agentry agent install --plan previews a persistent agent and its subagent pins; agent show lists its subagent runs.
agentry runhost set --unsafe-mode on makes every run on a runhost an Unsafe Mode run, with the admin sign-in.
A run on a runhost with Unsafe Mode on says so before it starts, and its envelope records it.
agentry runhost model --sign-in signs a runhost in to your Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot plan from your browser.
A run on a runhost can use that plan: Claude Code, Codex and Copilot CLI run in their images there, under gVisor.
agentry runhost store lists a runhost's sign-ins, and --remove ends one; agentry runhost remove ends them all.
A personal agent with Brave Search or Fastmail switched on starts again; 0.7.1 refused its stored key.
A run on a runhost whose credits token was revoked now says to give the runhost a new one, not to sign in.
A run now gets 30 minutes and no turn limit by default; you can still set a limit in the policy.
Setup builds Claude Code and Codex from their newest releases, checked against the vendors' signatures.
agentry draft writes persistent agents: the mode, only the capabilities they need, a persona and subagents.
agentry runhost model --provider agentry lets a runhost pay for its runs' models with your Agentry credits.
The runhost keeps a token that can only pay for model use, and agentry runhost store or remove revokes it.
A run on a runhost goes on there if your connection drops, and the CLI picks it up again where it was.
agentry runhost jobs, attach, collect and cancel reach a run on a runhost later; agentry run --on --detach leaves it.
agentry run --on runs an interactive session on a runhost, in the terminal chat or over --session-protocol.
A persistent agent can start runs of other QuickAgents as its subagents, each in a sandbox of its own.
Add a QuickAgent installed here as one with agentry agent configure --subagent; switch each off or ask first.
An agent run from the CLI can find, install, run and schedule QuickAgents, asking you first in agentry agent chat.
A persistent agent can now declare web search, AI Review and calendar feeds together.
The CLI, the desktop app, the MCP server and the Agentry server now share one version, 0.7.0.
It does everything 0.6.1019 does, with nothing removed.
agentry run --on now carries the rest of a local run: secrets, intake answers, files, knowledge packs and your voice.
A run on a runhost can reach a target host, use its MCP servers' sign-ins and deliver to your destinations from there.
When a runhost refuses a run, the exit code now says why (usage, verification or policy), as a local run's does.
An installed agent can run programs, browse and reach a dev server when its release declares the coding toolchain.
It can read your calendars, your mail at Google, Microsoft or Fastmail, and Google or Microsoft 365, as it declares.
It can search the web, each page read first by AI Review with your key, or ask AI Review about a package it holds.
agentry run --on runs a published QuickAgent on one of your remote runhosts and opens its sealed output here.
A persistent QuickAgent gets the time, tasks, a memory, skills and stored secrets only when its release declares them.
An installed agent can keep tasks that fire on time, a memory it compacts and recalls, and its own name and persona.
You can let an installed agent write in your Writing Voice; it is off until you switch it on.
When agentry runhost add or remove refuses a server's address or host key, the message names the runhost.
agentry agent install adds a persistent QuickAgent from the registry, or your own folder with --local.
An installed agent keeps its conversation and files between starts, and runs with the knowledge it ships.
It takes on the persona its publisher gave it, which you can rename and, unless locked, replace.
Two publishers' agents of the same name run side by side; agentry agent uninstall keeps their data unless asked.
agentry runhost add sets up a Linux server you own as a remote runhost, over SSH.
Setup checks the server first, then installs Docker, gVisor and this CLI, and opens no network port.
Your computer gets its own key for the runhost, which runs nothing but the runhost's service.
agentry runhost list, status, doctor and remove look after each runhost.
login, setup, install and validate end with the next step to take.
When the container engine or the registry cannot be reached, the CLI names which and how to fix it.
agentry doctor ends every failed check with a fix line and checks your sign-in, CLI version and PATH.
setup warns when the key variable is unset and defaults to each provider's newest model; --quiet and --verbose.
A run ends with a summary: its files, how long it took, what it cost where known, and where its receipts are.
A failed run names its exit class in words, the cause, the receipts folder, and whether a retry is likely to help.
agentry runs lists the runs made from here and agentry open opens one's folder; run --dry-run says the plan in words.
Every exit class has one name and meaning, shared by run --help, the summary and the result's JSON.
agentry info shows how to run a QuickAgent: its questions and how to answer each, its files, its keys and its guide.
agentry info --json carries the same, so an agent driving the CLI can answer the questions with --intake.
The Assistant and Agentry Helper work out how to run a QuickAgent from its own questions, files and guide.
Asked to run a QuickAgent on a repository, they give it the repository's address instead of asking you to download it.
Runs use the newest Docker Agent, MCP gateway and Codex, and every runtime image is rebuilt with current fixes.
Declared npm servers run on Node 26 and PyPI servers on Python 3.15, or on Python 3.14 when a server needs it.
A run stops before it starts when a tool filter names a tool in the wrong case, and says the exact name to use.
The Drafter's knowledge of the runtime is updated to match.
When a draft's instructions use a tool the agent was not given, the Drafter now fixes the draft before handing it back.
